subject: beetle
reasoning:
I'm planning a realistic stag beetle model at roughly life size, around 6cm long, oriented facing forward and standing on its legs with a root body joint near the base of its height.

For the mouth, I'm splitting it into a lower jaw piece and two large mandible joints for the signature stag beetle antler-like jaws. For the body, I'm laying out the head, pronotum (thorax), and split elytra (wing cases) with hinge joints, working out their positions and widths along the length of the body in millimeter-scale measurements.

I'm setting the leg length and body height so the beetle sits low to the ground, then planning to build each body segment from scaled sphere geometry with custom paint textures—chestnut-brown gradients and mottling for the elytra, darker tones for the pronotum. For the six legs, I'm thinking through using a chain of points (coxa, femur-knee, tibia-end, tarsus tip) swept along a curve for each pair.

Working out joint coordinates for each leg...

I'm adding small claw spikes at the tarsus tips and a couple on the front tibia, then adjusting the tip height and end radius so the feet just touch the ground plane without sinking too far below it.

Now I'm planning the antennae as geniculate chains with a small lamellate club, and sketching the head as a flattened wide sphere with dark eye spheres and mandible sweeps extending from the front.

I'm working through proportions for the stag beetle's mandibles versus body length, realizing my initial measurements make the creature too long overall, so I'm rescaling the head, pronotum, and elytra positions to keep the total body length realistic.

Still writing mandible path coordinates...

Still placing body parts...

Adding a scutellum triangle between pronotum and elytra, then a dark abdomen sphere tucked below, and a flattened pronotum sphere with a chestnut paint ridge up top. I'm also placing joint anchors for the body root and thorax to connect everything together.

Now I'm wiring up the hierarchy: thorax attached to the body, head attached to thorax, with eye spheres and highlights positioned near the jaw area. For coloring, I'm applying mottled chestnut gradients to the elytra and pronotum, and darker reddish-brown tones to the head and mandibles to give the exoskeleton a weathered, textured look.
